questions.question: Which folk music of Jammu and Kashmir is sung in wedding ceremonies?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - Wanawun**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wanawun**

 
 
• Wanawun is a traditional folk music genre from **Jammu and Kashmir.**
 
• It is primarily sung during wedding ceremonies.
 
• The songs in Wanawun are often celebratory and filled with blessings for the newlyweds and their families.
 
• This type of music creates a joyful atmosphere, enhancing the overall wedding experience.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Panihari**

 
 
• **Panihari is a type of folk music from Rajasthan.**
 
• It is traditionally sung by women while fetching water from wells or performing other daily chores.
 
• The songs often reflect the daily struggles, joys, and social issues faced by women in rural Rajasthan.
 
 
 
• **Alha**
 
 
• **Alha is a form of ballad singing from the Bundelkhand region in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• It involves narrating tales of bravery and heroism, often recounting the exploits of the legendary warriors Alha and Udal.
 
• Alha is not typically associated with wedding ceremonies but rather with festivals and gatherings.
 
 
 
• **Baul**
 
 
• **Baul is a form of mystic folk music from Bengal** (West Bengal in India and Bangladesh).
 
• Baul songs are characterized by their spiritual and philosophical themes, often focusing on love and devotion to God.
 
• This genre is more about individual spirituality and is not typically linked to wedding celebrations.

questions.question: Which of the following types of music is confined to the states of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Carnatic**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Carnatic Music__

 __
 
• Carnatic music is one of the forms of Indian classical music.
 
• It is confined to southern India, the states of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamilnadu, and Kerala
 
 
• ​ while the classical music of the rest of the country is under the name of Hindustani.
 
 
 
• The main emphasis in Carnatic music is on the vocals.
 
• The music is created in the traditional octave form and the music is Kriti-based
 
 
• ​ and focuses more on the Sahithya or the lyric quality of the musical piece.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Music**

 
 
• **​**Hindustani music is a major form of classical music practised primarily in North India, dating back to the Vedic times.
 
• It is based on **ragas** (melodic frameworks) and **talas** (rhythmic cycles) with a strong emphasis on improvisation by the performer.
 
• Renowned figures like **Pandit Ravi Shankar**, **Ustad Zakir Hussain**, and **Kishori Amonkar** have popularized Hindustani music globally.
 
• Common instruments include the **sitar**, **tabla**, **sarod**, and **tanpura**.
 
 
 
• **Regional Music**
 
 
• **​**Regional music refers to folk and traditional music from different parts of India, reflecting the cultural diversity of various regions.
 
• **Bihu** (Assam), **Baul** (Bengal), **Lavani** (Maharashtra), and **Garba** (Gujarat) are popular forms of regional music.
 
• Unlike classical music, regional music often has simpler structures, with repetitive rhythms and lyrics rooted in everyday life
 
 
 
• **Classical Music**
 
 
• **​**Indian classical music is divided into two main traditions: **Hindustani (North Indian)** and **Carnatic (South Indian)**.
 
• Classical music often has spiritual undertones, used in temples and courts historically, and is meditative in nature.
 
• Well-known classical musicians include **MS Subbulakshmi** (Carnatic), **Bismillah Khan** (Shehnai), and **Zakir Hussain** (Tabla).

questions.question: Which of the following folk music of Chhattisgarh is based on the epic Mahabharata?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandavani**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandavani** is a traditional folk music form from Chhattisgarh that is based on the epic **Mahabharata**.
 
• It is a narrative singing style where the performer enacts stories from the Mahabharata, often accompanied by musical instruments such as the tambura and harmonium.
 
• This form of storytelling is characterized by its dramatic and expressive performance, where the singer uses both song and speech to convey the tales of the Pandavas.
 
• Pandavani is not just a musical performance but also a theatrical one, involving gestures, facial expressions, and sometimes even props.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pandavani** performers often belong to the **Bhajan Mandali** tradition, which is a group dedicated to performing devotional songs and stories.
 
• One of the most renowned Pandavani performers is **Teejan Bai**, who has received numerous awards for her contribution to this art form, including the **Padma Shri** and **Padma Bhushan**.
 
• The art form has been instrumental in preserving the oral tradition of the Mahabharata in the region, making it accessible to the local populace.
 
• Pandavani performances are usually held during festivals, special occasions, and in village gatherings, serving as a form of entertainment as well as cultural education.

questions.question: The Lucknow Gharana which came into existence in the time of Wajid Ali Shah was developed by who among the following?

• It emphasizes storytelling through dance and has contributed significantly to the classical dance heritage of India.
 
• This Gharana has produced many renowned artists who have carried forward its rich traditions.

• The Lucknow Gharana is distinct from other Kathak Gharanas like the Jaipur and Banaras Gharanas, each having its own unique style and repertoire.
 
• Besides dance, the Lucknow Gharana has also influenced music, particularly the thumri style of singing.
 
• Efforts have been made to preserve and promote the traditions of the Lucknow Gharana through institutions and cultural festivals.

questions.question: Shattantri Veena, meaning a Veena with hundred strings, is the ancient Sanskrit name of which instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Santoor.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Santoor is a hammered dulcimer from the family of **string instruments**.
 
• The Santoor is primarily associated with **Indian classical music**, especially in the Hindustani tradition.
 
• **Pandit Shivkumar Sharma** has received the Padma Vibhushan and Padma Shri for their contributions to music.
 
• Santoor has gained popularity in contemporary and **fusion music** genres, showcasing its versatility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarod**

 
 
• A **fretless** string instrument with a deep, rich sound, typically made of wood and played with a plectrum.
 
• Renowned players include **Ustad Amjad Ali Khan** and **Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, **who have popularized the Sarod in Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Sarangi**
 
 
• A **bowed** string instrument known for its emotional expressiveness, often used in Hindustani classical music.
 
• Traditionally associated with vocal music accompaniment; famous players include **Ustad Sultan Khan** and **Pandit Ram Narayan**.
 
 
 
• **Tambura/Tanpura**
 
 
• A **long-necked** string instrument used primarily as a drone in Indian classical music, providing a harmonic foundation.
 
• Renowned musicians like **Ustad Vilayat Khan** and **Pandit Ravi Shankar** have included the Tanpura in their performances.
